title: Feature freeze capacity heatmap — May 2028
body:
Quick purpose:
This is a lightweight heatmap-style tracker to surface where we have tight slack during the planned feature freeze (2028-05-09 -> 2028-05-23). The goal is to call out 1) teams with <20% buffer vs estimated steady-state requests, 2) endpoints that may need temporary throttles or fallbacks, and 3) quick mitigation owners and actions we can take during the freeze window.

Notes about data and assumptions (short):
- Baseline traffic: 7-day moving average (2028-04-25 -> 2028-05-01) used as 'steady state' per endpoint.
- Capacity numbers shown are conservative — measured p99 token generation concurrency mapped to reserved GPU slots.
- We assume no model swaps during freeze unless emergency.
- 'Buffer %' = (allocated_capacity - estimated_peak)/allocated_capacity. Negative => overloaded.

Heatmap table (rows sorted by urgency):
| Priority | Team / Area                       | Endpoint / Route            | Est peak reqs/hr | Alloc slots | Buffer % | Short mitigation                    | Owner        | Action by | Risk (L/M/H) |
|----------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------|------------------:|-----------:|---------:|-------------------------------------|--------------|-----------|--------------|
| 1 (red)  | embeddings-serving                | /embed/batch                | 12,200           | 8          | -18%    | Burst to dedicated pool + cache key C | Aisha Patel  | 2028-05-05 | H            |
| 1 (red)  | realtime-chat                     | /chat/stream                | 9,400            | 6          | -10%    | Shorten max tokens, enable prefix cache| Ravi Menon   | 2028-05-04 | H            |
| 2 (amber)| search-rerank                     | /rerank                     | 6,500            | 5          | 0%      | Rate-limit non-paid clients 10%      | Tomás Alvarez| 2028-05-06 | M            |
| 2 (amber)| autocomplete                      | /suggest                    | 4,100            | 4          | 8%      | Increase batching window from 8→12ms  | Lena Ortiz   | 2028-05-07 | M            |
| 3 (green)| bulk-embeddings                   | /embed/bulk                 | 2,700            | 3          | 30%     | Defer non-urgent background jobs     | Eng infra    | 2028-05-10 | L            |
| 3 (green)| analytics-summaries               | /summarize                  | 1,200            | 2          | 40%     | Temporarily reduce sampling rate     | Product Ops  | 2028-05-08 | L            |

Quick one-line observations: 
- Embeddings batch route is highest pain point; heatmap flags need-for-dedicated-burst true positive in spike tests.
- Realtime chat's tail latencies drive slot contention; short token caps reduce p99 under the freeze.
- Bulk jobs are cheap to throttle and provide immediate buffer if needed.

Mitigation playbook (light checklist):
- Pre-freeze (by 2028-05-07):
  - Confirm burst pool capacity with Dedicated (ops) — owner: Eng infra.
  - Deploy prefix cache config change for realtime-chat to staging and run smoke — owner: Ravi.
  - Publish a short customer notice for non-SLAd bulk ingestion window changes — owner: Customer Success.

- During freeze (2028-05-09 -> 2028-05-23):
  - If buffer < 0 for any red endpoint: trigger immediate throttle for non-critical traffic (see routing playbook). Owner on-call for that team takes action.
  - If sustained overload after 30m: failover to fallbacks (lower-capacity model or region). Owner: team lead.

- Post-freeze (by 2028-05-25):
  - Revert temporary throttles and measure delta vs baseline. Owner: Product Ops.
  - Short retro: 15m cross-team sync to capture what worked. Owner: Lena.

Open questions / To decide quickly:
- Do we allow model variant swaps for emergency (yes/no)? (Suggested: no, only fallback variants).
- Will finance sign off on temporary burst credits for the embeddings pool? (Need approval).

Short action list (who does what):
- Aisha: validate burst pool sizing + test with 2x synthetic batches — due 2028-05-05.
- Ravi: land prefix cache change to staging + perf smoke — due 2028-05-04.
- Tomás: add non-paid-client 10% rate-limiter toggle flag and test — due 2028-05-06.
- Lena: brief cross-functional sync + publish the short ops playbook doc — due 2028-05-03.

Historic context (why created):
- Created after last-minute spikes in April 2028 caused two canary rollbacks. We want a minimal ops surface to avoid rollbacks during feature freeze.

Contact / escalation matrix:
- primary on-call infra: eng-oncall@redwood.com
- escalation: platform-leads@redwood.com

Revision log (notes):
- 2028-05-02 initial draft (Lena) — populated with 7-day avg numbers
- 2028-05-05 updated embedding slot estimates after load test (Aisha)
- 2028-05-08 added action owners and updated mitigation timing (Ravi)

Freeform notes (scratch):
- If finance denies burst credits we may need to shift lower-priority paid customers to scheduled windows (ugly, but doable).
- Consider adding a short 'customer-safe' banner that limits high-cost routes to opt-in during freeze.

End of doc.
